paragrafos: **Three measurements side by side, never added together.** Two prediction markets (Polymarket and Kalshi), voting-intention polls checked against the official notice filed with the Commission des sondages, and French press coverage. The first round is on April 18 and the runoff on May 2, 2027.

**On 11/17/2026, the two markets and the polls measure different things about Marine Le Pen.** In the win contract, Polymarket pays 46.45 and Kalshi 53.00. In polls with fieldwork up to 11/12, she is first in all 67 first-round lists of the last 45 days, from 8 pollsters, at 27% to 38%, and leads in the 32 runoff match-ups in which she was tested, at 52% to 70%. Her appeal to the Cour de cassation against her ineligibility is due to be ruled on by early April 2027.

**Jean-Luc Mélenchon is 2nd in the poll average and 3rd in the Polymarket win contract.** In the polls, he averages 17.7 across 36 lists from 5 pollsters over the last 30 days and places in the top two in 61 of the 67 lists of the last 45 days; in the 11 runoff match-ups in which he was tested, he trails in all of them, at 30% to 34%. In the win contract, he is at 13.50 on Polymarket and 12.00 on Kalshi.

**Two names among the top five in both markets appear in fewer than half of the lists in the poll database: David Lisnard in 25 of the 67 of the last 45 days, and Christine Lagarde in 2.** Lisnard is 2nd on Polymarket, at 16.05, and at 15.00 on Kalshi; in the polls, he does not place in the top two in any of his 25 lists and averages 8.1 across 18 lists from 5 pollsters over the last 30 days. Lagarde is 4th on Polymarket, at 7.10, and at 6.00 on Kalshi; the two lists that test her are by Cluster17 for Politico, with fieldwork on 11/09 and 11/10, and give her 14% and 8%. Lagarde is not a declared candidate; on 10/29, the European Central Bank announced that she will leave the bank's presidency on 02/07/2027. Teddy Riner, who announced his candidacy on 11/09, is at 2.05 on Polymarket and 1.00 on Kalshi; he appears in 2 of the 67 lists, at 2% in the Cluster17 one and 4% in the OpinionWay one for CNews, with fieldwork from 11/10 to 11/12. The Elabe poll for BFMTV and La Tribune Dimanche, with fieldwork on 11/12 and 11/13, which also tests him, already has an official notice and is not yet in the database.

**Édouard Philippe and Raphaël Glucksmann are close in the poll average and far apart in the Polymarket win contract.** Philippe averages 13.3 over the last 30 days, across 26 lists from 5 pollsters, and Glucksmann 12.4, across 34 lists from 5 pollsters; in the lists of the last 45 days in which they appear, Philippe places in the top two in 3 of 46, and Glucksmann in 3 of 62. In the win contract, Philippe is at 6.50 on Polymarket and 5.30 on Kalshi, and Glucksmann at 1.75 and 3.00.

**In the 18:25 UTC press collection of 11/16, four of the ten headlines, from 8 outlets, are about Marine Le Pen, three of them about Ukraine.** Les Echos, TF1 Info and BFMTV report that she stands by her position that, if elected, France would stop helping Ukraine financially; TF1 Info notes that she cites the state of public finances, and BFMTV that, according to her, France "would continue to support Ukraine". Le Figaro reports that she wants to scrap Parcoursup, the university admissions platform, and continuous assessment, and to move the baccalaureate exam forward to May. Three headlines are about the primary of the right and the centre: France 24 runs an analysis in which political scientist Bruno Cautrès, of Cevipof, calls the primary "an admission of failure" for Gabriel Attal and Bruno Retailleau; L'Opinion runs a piece on the number of candidates; and BFMTV reports that Gérard Larcher, president of the Senate, is calling on the candidates to meet to settle on a method for choosing between them. Le Parisien reports that, five months before the vote, one in two French people recognize themselves in a country that is "angry and highly contentious"; Ouest-France runs a video on a TF1-LCI debate devoted to purchasing power and precarity; and Le Figaro reports that actor Jean Reno will not take a position on the election.

**What this screen does not do.** It does not add or average the two markets, it does not turn a price into a voting intention, and it does not show a poll number without its checked official notice. On the Saturday and Sunday of each round, polls and prices are frozen, as French law of 1977 requires.
